status_summary: A USDA Food and Nutrition Service memo dated 2025-07-07, Guidance on the Interpretation of Discrimination Based on Sex in USDA Child Nutrition Programs, rescinds the May 2022 Bostock policy update and its related documents, cites Executive Order 14168, applies the 2020 Title IX rule and USDA's longstanding Title IX regulations, and ends pending compliance reviews based on the 2022 policy. The memo follows a 2025-07-02 settlement in which the Justice Department, for USDA, agreed to the rescission in exchange for dismissal of a Louisiana school board's lawsuit. No statute or government-wide rule barring all agencies from such withholding in the future was found. Separately, USDA froze some funds to Maine on 2025-04-02 in a dispute over the state's policy on transgender students in sports; a temporary restraining order in April and a court-approved settlement on 2025-05-02 ended the freeze. That episode involved a state with a gender-identity-inclusive policy and falls outside what this recommendation addresses.

timeline.event: USDA announced a freeze of some federal funds to Maine over the state's policy on transgender students in sports; a temporary restraining order in April 2025 barred the freeze pending further proceedings.
USDA and Maine reached a court-approved settlement under which USDA funds to the state may not be frozen.

The Justice Department, on USDA's behalf, executed a settlement with the Rapides Parish School Board dismissing its lawsuit against the 2022 policy in exchange for USDA rescinding it, as described in the USDA memo.

The FNS Administrator issued a memo rescinding the May 2022 Bostock policy update, its Q and A and cover letter, adopting a male-or-female reading of sex in child nutrition programs and ending pending compliance reviews based on the 2022 policy.
The National CACFP Sponsors Association reported the rescission to program operators.
